_comment: This repo's OWN declared ceilings for text a session loads before it
does any work. Repo-owned, never vendored: precedent_vendor_engine.py
lists this file as engine-READ but never engine-OWNED, so an engine
refresh will not overwrite the numbers below. They are mine to set.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL, 2026-09-11. The resident block is ONE
2000-token budget shared across every source a session resolves --
universal + team + individual combined -- and no practice SET can see
that total. precedent_resolve.py, which computes it, is in upstream's
CONSUMER_ENGINE_FILES and deliberately not in ENGINE_FILES: a set
resolves no catalogue, so it does not vendor the resolver. Each set
therefore measured only its own share, reported a healthy number, and
passed -- while the combined block sat at ~2047 tokens and overflowed.
Every local check was green the whole time.
resident_block_tokens below is this set's ALLOCATION of that shared
2000, not a private budget. It converts a global constraint nobody can
see into a local one build_views.py already enforces: it reads this key
in place of its 2000 literal and exits non-zero when the block exceeds
it. As long as every source's allocation sums to <= 2000, local green
implies global green -- which is the only way a set can police a budget
it cannot measure.
THE ALLOCATION, and the arithmetic behind it. After the 2026-09-11
demotions the combined block is ~1696 tokens across 15 resident
practices: this set ~351 (2 practices), precedent-individual ~468
(3), and ~877 across the remaining 10 from the universal source
and the other team sets. Allocations were set at roughly current + 18%
headroom, evenly applied:
precedent-individual           550   (currently ~468)
precedent-team-working-style   425   (currently ~351)
everything else, implied      1025   (currently ~877)
THE IMPLIED 1025 IS NOT DECLARED ANYWHERE, and that is this mechanism's
weak point, stated rather than hidden. Only the two sets above carry a
file like this one; the universal source and the other team sets keep
the 2000 default, so nothing stops their sum drifting past 1025 and
nothing here would notice. Re-derive the split whenever a source is
added or a practice changes tier, and treat these numbers as a running
hand-maintained agreement, not a computed fact.
The real gate remains very_deep_check.py's SESSION LOAD section, which
sums every attached source -- precedent_check.py's own session-load-budget
check says so in as many words -- but it runs only from a BestPractice
checkout with read access to these private sets. Until that runs on a
schedule, this file is the cheap approximation of it.
surfaces below is the SECOND, different budget: whole always-loaded
FILES rather than the resident block inside one. AGENTS.md and
CLAUDE.md are the surfaces this repo has (no .precedent/ -- see the
session-start-hook -> additionalContext channel note in
spec/PACK_SESSION_DOES_NOT_LOAD_UNIVERSAL.md in BestPractice).
IT IS DECLARED BUT NOT CURRENTLY CHECKED HERE, and saying so is the
point of writing it down. precedent_check.py reads surfaces only when
its session-load-budget check is in force, and that check reports
SKIPPED in this repo -- there is no practices/session-load-budget.md,
because the practice belongs to the universal source, which a practice
SET does not resolve. So nothing reads the ceiling below today. It is
declared anyway, for the repo that does resolve that practice and for
the day this set does: a measured number recorded now beats one
invented later, and an undeclared surface is how the resident block
overflowed in the first place.
resident_block_tokens above is the half that DOES bite here, and it was
verified rather than assumed: set temporarily to 300 against a ~351
block, build_views.py exits 1 with "over the 300-token hard cap".

AGENTS.md._note: Re-derived 2026-09-23 to 1,346 (measured) + ~20%, the final state of one day's churn: a cross-repo practice-placement review moved 4 practices in from precedent-individual (assorted-notes, content-directory) and demoted 2 from universal (answer-first-ask-before-long-work, their-constraints-are-given) -- landed, reverted same-day when the demotion broke a plain consumer's resolution (precedent_move.py had no safe path for --from universal yet), then re-landed properly once precedent_move.py gained one (duplicate-then-deliberately-dedupe, --accept-reach-loss). This set was genuinely thin (2 of 4 practices) and the original 1000 ceiling was sized for that. Was ~832 tokens on 2026-09-11, ceiling 1000 then.

CLAUDE.md._note: 111 tokens on 2026-09-20, the day the file was added -- the Claude Code adapter stub (@AGENTS.md include plus its explanatory comment), from templates/harness/claude-code/CLAUDE.md in BestPractice. Ceiling matches BestPractice's own CLAUDE.md surface entry, used as the model here.
